record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.context_brief: Adam conjecture for Euler oriented graphs
record.original_question: For an Euler oriented graph, meaning a connected oriented graph in which every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree, that contains at least one directed cycle, is there always an arc whose reversal decreases the total number of directed cycles?

evidence.quote: which claims that every oriented graph (i.e., a digraph without cycles of length 2), which has a cycle (in this paper all cycles and paths in digraphs are directed), contains an arc whose reversal decreases the number of cycles.
It seems to us that another interesting case is that of Euler oriented graphs, i.e., oriented graphs in which the in-degree of every vertex equals its out-degree;
A directed multigraph is Euler if it is connected and for every vertex x ∈ V (D), d +(x) = d−(x).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a directed multigraph $D=(V,A)$ an Euler oriented graph if (i) $D$ is connected, (ii) $D$ contains no pair of opposite arcs (i.e., no directed cycle of length 2), and (iii) every vertex $x\in V$ satisfies $d^{+}(x)=d^{-}(x)$, where $d^{+}(x)$ and $d^{-}(x)$ denote the out-degree and in-degree of $x$. A directed cycle in $D$ is a cyclic sequence $v_0,v_1,\dots,v_{k-1},v_0$ of distinct vertices with $(v_i,v_{i+1\bmod k})\in A$ for all $i$. For an arc $a=(u,v)\in A$, the reversal of $a$ replaces $a$ by $(v,u)$, yielding a new directed graph $D^{a}$. Let $c(D)$ denote the total number of directed cycles in $D$.

Prove or disprove: for every Euler oriented graph $D$ with $c(D)\ge 1$, there exists an arc $a\in A$ such that $c(D^{a})<c(D)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Ádám's original conjecture (for arbitrary oriented graphs with a directed cycle) has known counterexamples among general digraphs, but it remains open for several restricted classes, including tournaments and simple digraphs, with only partial results (e.g., Jirásek's result for digraphs becoming acyclic after at most three arc reversals, and the case of quasi-acyclic digraphs). The specific variant restricted to Euler oriented graphs does not appear to have been resolved in the literature, and no counterexample or proof was located.

status_evidence.snippet: Thesis discussing Ádám's conjecture and partial results on arc reversal reducing the number of directed cycles.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey/research on cycle structure in digraphs, including arc reversal type problems.
status_evidence.claim: The literature continues to address arc-reversal questions for digraphs, suggesting the Euler-oriented variant has not been settled.
